Avian Flu Outbreak Disrupts Vietnamese Banking Industry Operations

A recent outbreak of avian influenza has disrupted operations across Vietnam’s banking sector, with industry sources reporting absenteeism rates as high as 15% at some branch offices and call centers since the start of June. According to the Vietnam Banking Association, the outbreak, which was first identified among staff at Northern Capital Bank’s Hanoi headquarters, has since affected at least nine major urban branches across multiple cities.

“Many of our employees are currently on sick leave, and several branches have had to reduce operating hours or temporarily suspend in-person services,” said Le Thi Hong, spokesperson for the association. “We are working closely with health authorities and have implemented enhanced sanitation protocols at all affected sites.”

Several banks, including Phuc An Commercial Bank and Lotus Savings, have moved to remote work arrangements for administrative and back-office functions, though front-line customer service roles remain impacted. Managers at multiple institutions have reported delays in account processing and loan approvals, with one Ho Chi Minh City branch manager stating, “We’re doing our best to maintain service quality, but processing times are longer than usual due to staff shortages.”

Unions have called for additional protective measures and hazard pay for employees required to work on-site. “Our members are concerned for their health and well-being,” said Tran Van Minh, chair of the National Bank Workers’ Union. “We urge all banks to prioritize staff safety and provide necessary support.”

According to data compiled by the Vietnam Banking Association, over 1,200 workers have tested positive since the outbreak began, with the majority experiencing mild symptoms, but several hospitalizations have been reported. The association is advising all banking firms to maintain flexible staffing plans and ensure adequate protective equipment as the situation continues to develop.
